_headerComment: QWEN 3.8 NATIVE-MTP TRACK MANIFEST (track id qwen3.8-27b-mtp-v1).
TWO FILES, ONE CONTENT. benchmark.json is the manifest the Yukon CLI, the
modifiable-surface enforcement and the editable-path overlay read by default.
benchmark.qwen-mtp.json is a byte-identical copy under the track-qualified name,
and the ranked workflow names it explicitly through
MLXFAST_QWEN_MTP_EDITABLE_SURFACE_CONTRACT. Edit both or neither: a difference
between them is a bug.
JSON carries no comment syntax, so this note is a data field. It is inert:
nothing reads it, and every consumer reads the keys below by name.
THE TRACK IS LIVE AND SCORING. The contract fixture named by contractPath carries
official_scoring_enabled=true and reference_baseline.publication_allowed=true. The
ranked workflow ships MLXFAST_QWEN_MTP_CALIBRATION_READY=1, and every hidden and
public artifact pin holds a real digest. The track serves from the public
production repository Layr-Labs/qwen-3.8-mtp-challenge.
BACKBONE IDENTITY: the reference checkpoint is OUR OWN mlx-0.32.0 conversion of
the official bf16 base Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B @
1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0, MLX 4-bit affine group_size 64. It is
published as EigenLabs/Qwen3.8-27B-4bit @
eda45ab47f465d08d6558f0353a2346e2eb9d5b3 and pinned by the 10 records in
fixtures/reference_qwen3_8_27b_4bit.sha256. It replaced a third-party conversion
adopted earlier the same day and terminated by the operator's validation
kill-switch (994 of 1,847 tensors differed numerically from our reconversion);
the termination is recorded in the contract fixture's upstream_source_note.
MTP HEAD: EigenLabs/Qwen3.8-27B-MTP-bf16 @
26a328e070875b0314d652a039b6b59902690f03, 15 bf16 tensors, pinned by the 4
records in fixtures/qwen3_8_27b_mtp_head.sha256. The published tree also carries
config.json and model.safetensors.index.json, because the head loader refuses to
run without them.
BOTH CHECKPOINT REPOSITORIES ARE PUBLIC. They download anonymously, and no
Hugging Face token is required.
CALIBRATION IS 3.8. The timed pool and the on-box baseline were re-measured on
the Qwen 3.8 tower across six gated sessions on both ranked boxes. An unmodified
tree medians 0.9940390645 raw, so the shipped depth-2 configuration is a ~0.6%
regression against true serial decode. The floor (0.90) and the ceiling (3.0)
below are operator decisions and are unchanged. The contract fixture's
calibration block carries the per-prompt ratios and their provenance.
docs/qwen-mtp-go-live-runbook.md records the 3.6 go-live procedure that the 3.8
bring-up re-ran; its ids and numbers are 3.6-era.
CONTRACT CHANGE 2026-08-14 (operator-ratified). The competitive surface is the
UNION of MLX runner/kernel optimisation -- what the challenge family has always
been -- AND the whole speculative apparatus: head weights (mtp-head.manifest.json
+ mtp-head/), drafting code (Sources/MLXFastModel), and draft depth/schedule,
which the trusted driver no longer dictates. Scoring is re-anchored at SERIAL =
1.0: the published score is the median of the eight per-prompt RAW
serial-relative speedups, floored at 0.90 and ceilinged at 3.0; the pool's no-op
references stay pinned as informational diagnostics and no longer divide the
score. The definitive editable-vs-trusted table is
docs/qwen-mtp-editable-surface.md.
name: mlxfast-challenge-dev-qwen38-mtp
description: Qwen 3.8 27B native-MTP speculative-decode track: make the checkpoint's own multi-token-prediction head decode faster without changing a single emitted token. The competitive surface is a UNION of two things. First, and as in every track of this family, the MLX runner and kernel path: the Qwen 3.8 text tower, the offline transform, and the vendored MLX/Metal kernel families the forward pass dispatches. Second, the WHOLE speculative apparatus: the drafting code (Qwen36MTPBlockSession and its siblings), the draft depth and per-round schedule -- adaptive policies and non-drafting rounds are legal, bounded only by a trusted maximum of 8 drafts per round -- and the MTP HEAD WEIGHTS themselves, declared through mtp-head.manifest.json and fetched or shipped in-branch under mtp-head/. What stays fixed is the organizer-pinned TARGET checkpoint and its transform contract, the tokenizer, the goldens, and the verify/accept/ledger machinery. That split is not a compromise, it is the safety argument: anything that only PROPOSES tokens is safe by construction, because the trusted parent re-checks every emitted token against the hidden serial trajectory and closes the row ledger over the drafts actually proposed. Decode-only paired scoring against the TRUE serial control (MTP depth 0) on the same box, in the same session: the published score is the median of the eight per-prompt raw serial-relative speedups, so serial itself is exactly 1.0 (an unmodified tree medians ~0.994 on Qwen 3.8, measured across six gated calibration sessions). Native MTP decode is measured exact-greedy against serial on this checkpoint (12/12 runs to 512 tokens, all EOS branches), so the fidelity gate requires exact token match rather than a near-tie budget.
optionalEditablePathsNote: Editable paths a submission may legitimately OMIT. Submissions arrive as archives with REPLACE semantics over editablePaths -- whatever the archive does not carry is deleted -- and the head-declaration contract says an ABSENT mtp-head.manifest.json means the organizer-pinned head. Most archives will not carry one, so absence has to be the clean default rather than an overlay refusal: .github/scripts/overlay-editable-paths.sh skips a missing OPTIONAL path and keeps the trusted checkout's copy (which declares source=pinned), instead of failing closed the way it does for a missing SOURCE file, where absence really does mean a stale clone. The list is read from the TRUSTED contract, so a submission cannot make its own missing sources optional.

editableSurfaceByteBudget.note: The editable-surface byte budget (3 MB total / 512 KiB per file, enforced by .github/scripts/run-submission-static-review.sh and re-enforced at worker launch by EditableSurfaceByteBudget in Sources/MLXFastTrustedHarness) exists to stop a submission smuggling lookup tables in as SOURCE. Head WEIGHTS are not source, and the 2026-08-14 contract change makes them editable, so the one path that carries them is exempted from the code budget and given its own 2 GiB cap instead. The exemption is a path list, not a mode: every other editable path stays under the code budget, and an exempt path is excluded from the reviewed payload rather than reviewed cheaply -- a judge cannot read safetensors anyway. Digest and byte-count verification of the declared head (mtp-head.manifest.json) is what bounds this path, not the reviewer.

scoring.mtpMaxDraftDepthNote: OPERATOR-RATIFIED 2026-08-14. The track no longer pins a draft depth. The trusted parent offers a per-round ceiling and the CANDIDATE decides how many tokens it actually drafts -- 0 to 8, per round, adaptively if it likes. 8 is MLXFastConstants.qwenMTPMaxDraftDepth, a TRUSTED constant: it bounds the verify width a round may ask the target for, which is the only reason a bound exists at all. Depth was previously pinned at 2 with the note that it MUST be re-derived across the whole pool; opening it to the candidate is the re-derivation, moved from the operator to the competitor. Every ledger-closure and bit-exactness rule is derived from the ACTUAL draft count of each round, never from a declared depth, and the effective per-round counts are ledgered and summarised (effective_mean_draft_len, effective_max_draft_len, non_drafting_round_count) in the sealed report.
scoring.mtpEmptyDraftRoundsLegalNote: A round that drafts nothing is LEGAL and commits exactly its primary -- the shape an adaptive policy needs when it predicts the head will miss. Under serial-anchored scoring this games nothing: a candidate that never drafts IS serial and scores 1.0. The old refusal (stopTokenInsideWindow on a drafts-empty round) existed to protect a normalised denominator that no longer exists.
scoring.aggregationNote: OPERATOR-RATIFIED 2026-08-14, superseding the per-prompt normalised aggregation of 2026-08-13. A ranked run times ALL 8 contractPath timed_prompt_pool prompts. Each prompt gets its own RAW ratio-of-means -- mean serial (depth-0) seconds/token over that prompt's accepted pairs divided by mean candidate seconds/token over the same pairs -- and the published score is the MEDIAN of those 8 raw ratios. No normalisation step remains in the scoring path.
scoring.medianRuleNote: 8 is EVEN, so this is load-bearing: the score is the mean of the two central order statistics, NOT the lower-median rule the per-pair mtp_decode_speedup_median diagnostic uses.
scoring.scoreAnchorNote: Normalising by each prompt's pinned no-op reference made an UNMODIFIED CANDIDATE score exactly 1.0 by construction, which silently declared the shipped depth-2 speculative decoder to be the zero point. It is not: measured on the Qwen 3.8 tower it is a ~0.6% regression against true serial decode at the 512-token window (raw median 0.9940390645). Anchoring at serial makes the leaderboard read as physics -- 1.0 is serial decode, above 1.0 is a real speedup, and the shipped configuration starts below the line with work to do. It also makes the whole speculative apparatus safely editable: a candidate that drafts nothing degenerates to serial and scores 1.0, so 'turn speculation off' is a legal, honest, unremarkable submission rather than an exploit.
scoring.noopReferenceRoleNote: contractPath timed_prompt_pool[].noop_decode_speedup is RETAINED and still pinned, but it no longer participates in scoring. It is the measured depth-0-over-depth-2 ratio of the pinned baseline tree per prompt (0.7623 to 1.0845), which is exactly the per-prompt regression profile of the SHIPPED configuration -- useful for reading a per-prompt breakdown, and reported alongside every prompt's raw ratio, but not a divisor. The score's own per-prompt normalisation is what it always should have been: the serial leg measured in the same session, in the same pair.
scoring.decodeSpeedupFloorNote: Applied to the RAW median and pinned EQUAL to MLXFAST_QWEN_MTP_DECODE_SPEEDUP_FLOOR in the ranked workflow, which is the enforcing site; this field is documentation and is not itself enforced. OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-14: 0.90, "do not regress serial by more than 10%". WHY NOT 0.95, THE FAMILY CONVENTION: at 0.95 this track could not launch. Yukon's import dispatches a BASELINE RUN OF THE SOURCE TREE and needs a published score to seed currentBestScore; no score means the benchmark never opens and no submission can ever be made. The stock tree medianed ~0.935 raw on Qwen 3.6 -- a measured ~6.5% regression against true serial decode, which is the fact serial anchoring exists to stop hiding -- so a 0.95 floor rejected the one run the track bootstraps from. The 0.95 convention came from a NORMALISED score where an unmodified tree sat at 1.0 by construction and does not survive the change of anchor. WHAT 0.90 MEANS: a regression bound, not a quality bar -- a submission may be slower than serial and the board will say so, but not by more than 10%; a candidate that cannot beat serial should stop drafting and take 1.0, which is legal, free and strictly better than publishing 0.92. CONSEQUENCES: on the Qwen 3.8 tower the stock tree publishes 0.994 and holds the board at -0.6%; calibration dispatches publish normally; k3-class regressions (~0.777) still floor-fail. Operator-confirmable default.
scoring.decodeSpeedupCeilingNote: ADDED 2026-08-14 (k-matrix finding 3: the published aggregate had a floor and no ceiling, so an implausible median could only be caught per-pair by the box wrapper's MAX_PLAUSIBLE_SPEEDUP and never at the published number). RAISED 3.0 -> 5.0 by operator decision 2026-08-17, with the wrapper's per-pair bound raised 5.0 -> 8.0 in the same decision so the aggregate ceiling stays strictly tighter than the per-pair bound. A plausibility bound on the PUBLISHED median: 5.0. Generous by construction -- the authors' own exact-greedy envelope tops out at 1.74x at a 32-token window, kernel work on this tower has historically bought tens of percent, and 5.0 leaves room for both compounding -- so a number above it is a measurement fault or an escape, not a result. Enforced in the trusted workflow alongside the floor; the box wrapper enforces the same value on the aggregate as well as its per-pair bound. Operator-confirmable default.
scoring.pairsPerPromptNote: PER PROMPT, not per run: a ranked run is 8 prompts x 1 pair = 8 pairs / 16 timed phases. Supersedes the run-level minAcceptedPairs 3 / targetPairs 4, which bought pair-averaging on a single prompt; the median over 8 prompts does that job and also cancels the prompt lottery. Raisable via the measurement wrapper's --pairs-per-prompt when calibration data asks for it.
scoring.stallGuardrail: max block latency > 4x p50 rejects the run (one gated retry)
